title: Remote Targets and Fleet Boundary
objective: Extend observation/governance to remote development environments without weakening local authority or OSS boundaries.

stories.title: Remote target abstraction
stories.outcome: Model SSH/dev-container/CI-runner targets as explicit machines with independent capabilities and trust.
stories.risk_reclassification_note: Declared CR2 at planning time; raised to CR3 at commit time because the change adds rust/crates/cancellai-model/src/remote_target.rs - the domain-model floor project/risk_floors.json sets for rust/crates/cancellai-model/src/*, since it defines what an artifact, an authority and a plan are and every downstream decision is expressed in its types, even though this change is purely additive and does not touch AgentArtifact or any existing type.
acceptance_criteria: Remote inventory never masquerades as local state.
Disconnected targets preserve last-seen state as stale, not current.

stories.title: Local-agent remote execution boundary
stories.outcome: Keep mutation execution on the target node under its local safety kernel even when a remote controller requests policy evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Remote control cannot bypass target safety invariants.
Every remote request is authenticated, authorized, and audit-linked.

stories.title: OSS/commercial protocol boundary
stories.outcome: Define an open local node protocol and separate optional fleet-control services without reducing local functionality.
stories.risk_reclassification_note: Declared CR1 at planning time; raised to CR4 at commit time because the change adds a test to rust/crates/cancellai-safety/src/remote_execution.rs - the safety-kernel floor project/risk_floors.json sets for rust/crates/cancellai-safety/src/*, since every mutation decision passes through this crate (C-07), even though the added test only exercises an already-covered path (effective_authority with an unused, empty TrustedRemoteControllers) and adds no new production logic. The CR4 reclassification also triggered scripts/check_ears.py's requirement that a CR2+ story name unwanted behaviour; AC3 below was added at commit time as the EARS-compliant restatement of AC1's existing intent, not new scope.
acceptance_criteria: Single-machine workflows remain fully functional without account/cloud.
Commercial services add coordination, not local destructive capabilities.
If no commercial or fleet-coordination service is configured or reachable, single-machine functionality is not reduced or refused.
